question: Among the stages of rounds 1 and 2 grown by the census's law from every legal meet-once arrangement of at most 7 junctions, are there non-isomorphic pairs with isomorphic full bond-distance tables and other allowed states?

definitions.key: table read to 8, pooled beyond, WL hash
definitions.depth: self-grown depth (peel, regrow one round, compare), at most 4

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py --out runs/grow-small2 (8 workers, 16G cap); .venv/bin/python -B pairs_grow.py runs/grow-small2; .venv/bin/python -B targeted.py
public_inputs.reused: PARENT-RULE-20261119-001B plib.py, census_job.py, static_job.py, static_pairs.json; MEET-ONCE-20261119-001A pairs_meet2.py

forbidden_inputs: Changing G1, G2, C0, K after the runs
cheapest_meaningful_control: C0: the 472 static other-states groups recovered by the same pairing

predictions.K: meet once; every open stage of round r has depth >= r; relabelled copies isomorphic

amendments.when: after the first launch stalled (28 minutes, one case), before any stage of the run was read; targeted.py had already run and been read
amendments.change: arrangement isomorphism and hash on the junction graph with loose and shared counts (job.py sha256 99e6a5b1688d5c0d245fef76e38286849ab060cfcc857bec9caa472137ce6768, pairs_grow.py sha256 4b240252e2531866338de06ff23ddbdca03a53df30c2dc3ace10980ef9a6c047); K's depth clause restricted to open stages
amendments.unchanged: G1, G2, C0, the population, the pairing, targeted.py
